coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P10
names: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P10
P10 -- landscaped center island, Mission Bay Circle roundabout
record.summary: P10 is a park parcel labelled on OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, tracked here as the landscaped center island of the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout (the map draws the label 'P10' on the circular island inside the ring labelled 'MISSION BAY CIRCLE'; EPA's July 2012 fact sheet names 'Park P10 and Mission Bay Circle' together as one funded construction project). OCII's September 2023 open-space transition presentation lists P10 among the parcels the Recreation and Parks Department will manage, not among the 'when built' parcels; the presentation is a plan and does not itself say whether P10 was complete. The City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement lists P10 among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and says P10, P11 and P11A 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works); the draft says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay Parks, but not who built this parcel, and no signed text of the agreement was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- hand-traced from satellite imagery, not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. Deliberately not trimmed back from the street lines: this is a real roundabout center island, ringed by the circulating roadway in DataSF's street data -- trimming it against the standard street buffer would cut real, visible parts of the island, not correct a mispositioning. lot 8709003 (1400 Owens St per DataSF, MB-RA zoning, recorded 1999-09-21, active, 12,999 m2) lies under this island and its neighbours. Pier & Point reads it as split between P10 (the roundabout island), P8 and P7 or P9 across from P8; against our drawings it overlaps P8 by 3,603 m2, P10 by 983 m2, P7 by 3,431 m2 and P9 by 136 m2. P10 has no lot of its own, so the drawing is kept.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery), following an outline Pier & Point drew by hand on a marked-up screenshot, transferred onto the imagery by matching image features rather than re-estimated by eye -- the same technique used for P11/P11A.

open_questions: EPA's July 2012 brownfields fact sheet names "Mission Bay Park P10" (Subgrant 4, $760,000) for "the construction of Park P10 and Mission Bay Circle" and carries the photo caption "Landscaping and hardscaping enhance the look of Mission Bay Park P10"; it gives no start or completion year. EPA's November 4, 2011 advisory announces a tour "to celebrate the completion of Mission Bay Drive and Circle", while Bay Crossings (December 2011) calls Mission Bay Circle "a landscaped turnaround that will eventually serve as a gateway" and says a new road "will open in early-to-mid 2012"; those two sources differ on how finished the Circle was in November 2011. No source read dates the start or completion of the park itself.

Who built and who holds it: the City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement (recital D) lists P10, P11 and P11A among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and section 5(j) says they 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works), with any CFD funds used by RPD to maintain them on PW's behalf or passed to PW. Recital C says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay parks; no source read says who built these three parcels. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo says the Board would need to vacate the public right-of-way status on the park parcels, and the Board's December 5, 2023 resolution (File 231132) approved the agreement and said Port and RPD expected to seek the jurisdictional transfer by a separate ordinance in early 2024. No signed agreement, transfer ordinance or later source on these three parcels was found, so Public Works is the holder per the draft only.

As of 2026-09-29, no source read dates the start or completion of Park P10 itself. The July 2012 EPA fact sheet (undated construction, 'projected' workers) and the Nov 2011 EPA advisory (completion of 'Mission Bay Drive and Circle') do not separate the island; the earlier '2010 under construction' milestone had no source for its year and was removed, and the Nov 2011 milestone's 'under construction' status was removed because the EPA advisory contradicts it.

Whether Park P10 is only the roundabout's center island is unconfirmed: EPA's fact sheet gives $760,000 for 'the construction of Park P10 and Mission Bay Circle' together, which looks large for an island alone. The 'landscaped with grass and trees' description rests on Pier & Point's reading of satellite imagery, not a document.
